title: Design Twitter
prompt:
Design a tiny Twitter:

- `Twitter()`
- `void postTweet(int userId, int tweetId)`: each call uses a unique `tweetId`
- `List<Integer> getNewsFeed(int userId)`: the 10 most recent tweet ids posted by the user or anyone they follow, newest first
- `void follow(int followerId, int followeeId)`
- `void unfollow(int followerId, int followeeId)`

**Example**: user 1 posts 5; feed(1) → `[5]`; 1 follows 2; 2 posts 6; feed(1) → `[6,5]`; 1 unfollows 2; feed(1) → `[5]`.

tests.note: only 10 newest; unfollowing yourself keeps your own tweets

hints: A feed mixes tweets from several users. What do you need to store with each tweet so tweets from different users can be put in order?
Keep a global counter as a timestamp, a per-user list of `{time, tweetId}`, and a per-user set of followees. For a feed, only the last 10 tweets of each relevant user can matter.
Merge those candidate tweets with a max-heap ordered by time and poll up to 10. Always include the user's own tweets, even if they follow or unfollow themselves.

solution.explanation: A single increasing timestamp orders tweets across all users. Each user's list is already sorted by time, so only its last 10 entries can reach the feed, and a heap merges these short lists into the 10 newest overall. The feed costs O(f · 10 · log(10f)) for f followees; post, follow and unfollow are O(1). Space O(users + tweets + follows).
